_meta.description: Curated catalog of OpenSCAD library components for parametric generation

backlash.description: thins this gear's teeth by this much along the pitch circle, in mm; a pair made with the same value has twice that play

shaft_diam.description: center shaft hole diameter in mm

spur_gear.agent_guidance: Meshing gears share circ_pitch and pressure angle. Use 17 or more teeth where the design allows; gears of 17 teeth or fewer are profile-shifted by default, so place a pair with gear_dist(teeth1=, teeth2=, circ_pitch=) rather than the sum of the pitch radii. Always give backlash: it defaults to zero and printed teeth come out fat. Calculate teeth ratio for speed reduction. A printed gear that carries torque on a shaft needs a D, hex or keyed bore, not a round press fit.
spur_gear.printability_notes: Print flat. Teeth under circ_pitch=4.7 (module 1.5) do not print cleanly on a 0.4mm nozzle.

mate_teeth.description: number of teeth on the mating gear

shaft_diam.description: center shaft hole diameter in mm

bevel_gear.agent_guidance: mate_teeth must match the paired gear. Both gears need same circ_pitch. Give backlash: it defaults to zero. A bevel pair is the gear pair most sensitive to where it is mounted: one 0.2 mm layer of error in where a gear sits along its shaft changes the pair's play by about 0.1 mm, so make that position adjustable or test-fit it.
bevel_gear.printability_notes: Print with flat back on bed. May need supports for tooth undercuts.

width.description: distance from the base of the rack to the tips of its teeth, in mm

rack.agent_guidance: Use the same circ_pitch and pressure angle as the mating spur_gear. Give backlash on the rack and the gear: it defaults to zero and printed teeth come out fat. Put the gear's axis gear_dist(teeth1=<gear teeth>, teeth2=0, circ_pitch=) from the rack's pitch line; a gear of 17 teeth or fewer is profile-shifted and sits farther out.
rack.printability_notes: Print flat. Long racks may need bed adhesion help.

worm_starts.description: number of thread starts on worm

worm_gear.agent_guidance: Pair with worm() module for the worm shaft. High gear reduction. Never rely on a printed worm drive to hold a load: it can back-drive, and grease or vibration make that more likely. Where a load must not move or fall, add a brake, a ratchet or a one-way clutch.
worm_gear.printability_notes: Print worm gear flat. Worm shaft prints on side.

d.description: outer (major) diameter in mm: 8 for M8

pitch.description: thread pitch in mm: the distance from one crest to the next

threaded_rod.agent_guidance: M8x1.25 is d=8, pitch=1.25. Standard metric coarse pitches: M3=0.5, M4=0.7, M5=0.8, M6=1.0, M8=1.25. Pair with threaded_nut at the same id and pitch. The printing clearance goes on the nut ($slop); $slop does not change a rod.
threaded_rod.printability_notes: Print vertically. Pitch under 1.0mm requires a fine nozzle.

nutwidth.description: flat-to-flat width of the hex (the wrench size): 13 for an M8 nut

id.description: nominal size of the thread, the diameter of the rod or screw it takes: 8 for M8 (measured at the thread roots, not across the hole's narrowest point)

$slop.description: printing clearance: widens the thread by 4 x $slop on the diameter. At 0 the nut's thread touches the rod's everywhere, leaving no room for the printed surfaces

threaded_nut.agent_guidance: id and pitch must match the threaded_rod: id is the nominal size (8 for M8), not the hole's inner diameter. nutwidth is across the flats, not a diameter. $slop=0.15 leaves 0.3 mm of radial clearance at the crests and roots; tune it to the printer, and never widen id as well. nut("M8") from BOSL2/screws.scad makes the standard ISO nut (13 across the flats, 6.8 mm tall) and takes $slop the same way.

spec.description: size, then length after a comma: "M5,20" is M5, 20 mm long. A pitch goes after an x ("M5x0.8,20"), so "M5x20" asks for a 20 mm pitch and fails

head.description: head type: socket, hex, flat, button, pan

drive.description: recess in the head: hex, torx, phillips, slot, or none (socket and button heads take hex or torx)

screw.agent_guidance: Leave the pitch out of spec for the standard coarse thread (M5 is 0.8). Length is measured under the head, so "M5,20" with a socket head is 25 mm overall; a flat head's length includes the head. Without drive the head has no recess. The thread is made to the standard screw tolerance, a little under nominal, so it fits a standard nut; a printed nut for it needs $slop. orient=DOWN, anchor=TOP stands the screw on its head for printing; leave them out to place it in an assembly.
screw.printability_notes: Print standing on the head, as the example call places it: the thread is vertical and nothing needs support (the key recess is bridged). Standing on its tip, the head's underside would hang in the air. Fine threads (M3 and below) are challenging on FDM.

screw_hole.agent_guidance: Use inside difference() to cut holes in parts. Counterbore hides the screw head.
screw_hole.printability_notes: Print with hole axis vertical for best roundness. Holes under 3mm may need drilling.

knuckle_hinge.agent_guidance: Print both halves. Use inner=true for the mating half. Add 0.2mm gap for clearance.
knuckle_hinge.printability_notes: Print flat. Knuckle segments need good layer adhesion.

snap_lock.agent_guidance: Pair with snap_socket for the mating part. Material matters — PLA snaps break, use PETG or nylon.
snap_lock.printability_notes: Print with snap arm in XY plane for layer strength.

ball_bearing.agent_guidance: Common sizes — 608 (skateboard), 624 (small), 625 (mini). This generates a model of the bearing for visualization/housing design.
ball_bearing.printability_notes: Not meant for functional printing — use as reference to design bearing housings.

linear_bearing.printability_notes: Print upright. Ensure wall thickness is sufficient for the bearing press-fit.

nema_stepper_motor.agent_guidance: Most common is NEMA 17 for 3D printers. Use nema_mount_mask() to create screw mounting holes.
nema_stepper_motor.printability_notes: Reference model for designing mounts — use nema_mount_mask() in difference().

joiner.agent_guidance: Use half_joiner and half_joiner2 for mating pairs. Print-in-place dovetail joints.
joiner.printability_notes: Print flat. Clearance built in for print-in-place assembly.
